target.contract: Input is {entries:[{id,type,content,timestamp}],filter:{type,since,search,limit}}. Timestamps/since are finite milliseconds; every filter field is nullable. Return complete matching entries in input array order. Preserve actual FX getMemory semantics: type and since filtering, case-insensitive substring search, and finite numeric limit behavior including negative, fractional, zero or null limits.

note: Steps are deterministic interpreter work units, not native time. No production activation.

limitations: Search is bounded by its proposal grammar; it does not claim globally novel algorithms.
Cost is interpreter steps, loop visits and allocated cells, not measured native speed.
Cost baselines are explicit IR implementations, not timings of the original FX or Rust code.
Memory correctness uses the actual FX getMemory function as its oracle.
The Beetle target is a synthetic batch reference model; native Rust conformance is still required.
The winner is exported as data and is never automatically deployed.
